title: VL-ThyNet: An interpretable analytical framework integrating visual foundation models and vision-language reasoning for malignancy risk assessment of C-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《VL-ThyNet: An interpretable analytical framework integrating visual foundation models and vision-language reasoning for malignancy risk assessment of C-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Accurate differentiation between benign and malignant C-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules is particularly challenging because of their intermediate malignancy risk and overlapping sonographic features, yet it is essential for clinical decision-making.

evidence.text: Accurate differentiation between benign and malignant C-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules is particularly challenging because of their intermediate malignancy risk and overlapping sonographic features, yet it is essential for clinical decision-making.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《VL-ThyNet: An interpretable analytical framework integrating visual foundation models and vision-language reasoning for malignancy risk assessment of C-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】On the test set, VL-ThyNet achieved an accuracy of 84.8% and an AUC of 0.902, showing higher ACC and AUC than the evaluated conventional CNN- and Transformer-based models.

【Abstract · abstract-1-8】In a reader study, VL-ThyNet assistance was associated with improved diagnostic accuracy among radiologists and an 18.4% reduction in the average image interpretation time of the six radiologists, indicating its potential as an interpretable and efficient auxiliary analytical tool for thyroid nodule assessment.

evidence.text: On the test set, VL-ThyNet achieved an accuracy of 84.8% and an AUC of 0.902, showing higher ACC and AUC than the evaluated conventional CNN- and Transformer-based models.

In a reader study, VL-ThyNet assistance was associated with improved diagnostic accuracy among radiologists and an 18.4% reduction in the average image interpretation time of the six radiologists, indicating its potential as an interpretable and efficient auxiliary analytical tool for thyroid nodule assessment.
